cases.statement: One person in the batch: the male proband of Family 1 in a Japanese nationwide survey (30413001). Table 1 also lists an affected male cousin, the affected mother and one affected sister, with no genotype stated for them.

people.label: proband (Family 1)
people.zygosity_or_genotype: not reported (sex implies hemizygous; zygosity not stated)
people.key_phenotypes: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mild myopathy without mental retardation (stated for the two affected males of Family 1); small amount of residual LAMP-2 protein

quotes.quote: | 1 | E9b | c.1097_1098 delAA | Frame shift | proband, 1 cousin | mother, 1 sister | [2] |
The two affected males in Family 1 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mild myopathy, but no mental retardation.
In addition, the proband in Family 1 revealed a small amount of LAMP-2 protein on immunoreactivity studies, as reported previously [1].

phenotype_specificity.statement: The two affected Family 1 males had HCM and mild myopathy without mental retardation; the authors suggest the exon 9b (LAMP-2b-only) defect gives a milder phenotype. One Family 1 man was alive at 50 with mild cardiomyopathy (the paper does not say whether this is the proband or the cousin). Testing of other genes is not reported.

quotes.quote: The two affected males in Family 1 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mild myopathy, but no mental retardation.

In this family, one male patient who had mild cardiomyopathy, but reported no cardiac symptoms is alive at the age of 50 years, although no male patient survived beyond the age of 26 years except for in this family.
Therefore, we suggest that the isolated deficiency of the LAMP-2b isoform may be associated with a milder phenotype, although we could not find a genotype–phenotype correlation, except for exon 9.

segregation.statement: Table 1 lists affected relatives in Family 1: 1 male cousin, the mother and 1 sister. The paper does not state whether any relative was genotyped for the variant; no unaffected relatives are described.

functional.statement: Patient tissue (immunoreactivity study, tissue not specified; reported previously in reference [1]): a small amount of LAMP-2 protein detected in the proband. No construct assay. The authors note that this variant affects only the LAMP-2b isoform.

quotes.quote: In addition, the proband in Family 1 revealed a small amount of LAMP-2 protein on immunoreactivity studies, as reported previously [1].
The mutation in Family 1 affects only the LAMP-2b isoform, whereas all other mutations affect both the LAMP-2a and 2b isoforms.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-base deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(Gln366ArgfsTer6) on the batch transcript). The paper places it in exon 9b, the LAMP-2b-specific exon, and calls it a frame shift. Authors state Danon disease is caused by loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: | 1 | E9b | c.1097_1098 delAA | Frame shift | proband, 1 cousin | mother, 1 sister | [2] |
LAMP-2a is present ubiquitously, whereas LAMP-2b is expressed predominantly in heart and skeletal muscles.
Danon disease is primarily caused by loss-of-function mutations in the LAMP-2 gene.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level statement: none of the survey's mutations was found in 100 Japanese controls.

quotes.quote: On screening 100 Japanese controls, the same mutations were not found.

concerns: The paper puts this variant in exon 9b (LAMP-2b-specific) and states no transcript. The batch maps it to NM_002294.3; the panel should confirm that this coordinate is the exon 9b position the paper means, because the alternative exon 9 forms have different c. numbering.
Survey table only: the case description is in the cited earlier report (reference [2], Sugie 2002), which is not in this batch.
Affected relatives (male cousin, mother, sister) are listed in Table 1 but not genotyped in the text and are not in the batch.
Residual LAMP-2 protein was reported for this proband, unlike the complete absence the paper reports in other male patients.

30413001 contradicts itself on recurrent variants: the text says Family 11 and Family 15 share c.877C > T, while Table 1 lists c.877C>T for Families 10 and 14, c.371_372 delCA for Family 11 and c.56T>C for Family 15.
30413001 gives two different counts for families whose mothers or relatives tested negative (eight families in Results, 10 families in Discussion) and does not say which families these are.
30413001 states no transcript and no protein change; c. numbering cannot be checked against NM_002294.3 from this paper alone.
notes_for_panel: 30413001 is a nationwide questionnaire survey; per-family information is limited to Table 1 (site, cDNA change, effect on mRNA, affected relatives, source reference). It gives no transcript, no protein change and no per-person phenotype table.
